extracted.intended_audience: FBI leadership, DOJ officials, field office supervisors, and law enforcement policy-makers
extracted.subtask_short: FBI handling of sexual abuse allegations
extracted.subtask_description: An Office of the Inspector General report reviewing how FBI field offices handled allegations of sexual abuse by Lawrence G. Nassar, with findings about policy violations and recommendations to change FBI practice for receiving, documenting, transferring, investigating, and reporting crimes against children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt contact/coordination with state and local authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: FBI employees must be required to promptly contact and coordinate with applicable state and local law enforcement and social service agencies after receiving allegations of crimes against children that potentially fall under state jurisdiction, even when the allegations also potentially fall within the FBI’s jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 1.a: clarify for FBI employees when prompt contact/coordination is required to mitigate ongoing danger; OIG found Indianapolis and Los Angeles offices failed to notify local authorities despite uncertainty about federal jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm receipt of transfers between field offices
rubrics_metrics.description: FBI employees must confirm receipt of transfers between field offices of certain categories of complaints, such as complaints of serious or multi-victim sexual abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 1.b: ensure FD-71 or transfer paperwork is actually received by the receiving office; OIG found no record that an FD-71 reached the Lansing Resident Agency after Indianapolis claimed to have sent it.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use Child/Adolescent Forensic Interviewers (CAFI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify when interviews by Child/Adolescent Forensic Interviewers (CAFI) should be conducted of children and adults reporting allegations of abuse they experienced as children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 1.c: define circumstances and timing for CAFI use to ensure developmentally appropriate interviews and better documentation/consistency across field offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer victim services during Pre-Assessment/Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the circumstances under which victim services should be offered during Pre-Assessment or Assessment activities, such as when these phases take longer than expected, when a victim is interviewed as part of these phases, or when an initial complaint is transferred between field offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 1.d: ensure victims receive support even prior to opening a formal investigation; OIG flagged lack of victim services during long pre-assessment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory approval rules for supervisor-conducted activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the type of approval required (including who must provide approval) when a supervisor conducts investigative activity or completes documentation that would require supervisory approval when conducted by a nonsupervisory Special Agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 2.a: prevent supervisors from self-authorizing or approving work they performed; FBI response also notes supervisors may not approve documentation they drafted themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Assessment time limit (5 days) — clarify
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify whether Pre-Assessment activities can continue for more than 5 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 2.b: current practice unclear; OIG suggests policy should state whether extension is allowed and under what circumstances, because extended pre-assessments can delay investigation and victim protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention/file type for documentation during extended Pre-Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: If Pre-Assessment activities continue for more than 5 days, specify what type of file FBI employees should use to retain documentation received during Pre-Assessment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 2.c: standardize recordkeeping for materials collected during pre-assessment so evidence and communications are preserved and discoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to open Assessment if Pre-Assessment exceeds allowed time
rubrics_metrics.description: If Pre-Assessment activities cannot be completed within allowed time, clarify whether employees should open an Assessment when they need more than 5 days to assess alleged federal violations and venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 2.d: reduce delays by requiring escalation to formal Assessment if initial evaluation takes too long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on telephonic interviews of alleged child abuse victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a policy describing the circumstances, if any, under which telephonic interviews of alleged child abuse victims, including adults who had allegedly been victims of abuse as children, are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 3: OIG criticized the decision to conduct Gymnast 1’s interview telephonically as poor judgment; policy should limit telephonic interviews and define exigent circumstances for use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on updated policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Train FBI employees on the policies discussed in the recommendations (coordination with local authorities, transfer confirmations, CAFI use, victim services, Pre-Assessment rules, telephonic interviews) and any changes made to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation 4: implement formal training programs so field personnel understand new/clarified expectations; FBI response describes updated annual training and development of mandatory supervisor training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documenting pre-assessment activities and meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Document meetings and pre-assessment activities (including initial receipt of allegations) promptly and thoroughly; maintain original interview notes and contemporaneous records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found Indianapolis failed to formally document the July 28, 2015 meeting, kept only limited handwritten notes, and delayed drafting an FD-302 for 17 months, resulting in inaccuracies; documentation should include attendees, materials received, and actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use and forwarding of FD-71 complaint form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use FD-71 complaint forms to transfer allegations between FBI jurisdictions and ensure the FD-71 is entered into the case management system and forwarded correctly to the receiving field office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG could not find an FD-71 in the system for the claimed 2015 transfer; policy should require confirmation and audit trail for FD-71 transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely documentation of interviews in FD-302 and maintenance of original notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Document victim and witness interviews promptly in FD-302 report format and retain original notes; co-interviewers should consult each other and source notes when preparing FD-302s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found the Indianapolis SSA drafted an FD-302 17 months after the interview using limited notes and memory, producing materially false/omitted statements. Guidance: contemporaneous notes, joint preparation or review, and timely FD-302 completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling and documentation of evidence (e.g., thumb drives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly handle, document chain of custody, and preserve electronic and physical evidence received during initial meetings or pre-assessment activities (for example, thumb drives containing videos or slides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found the Indianapolis SSA failed to properly handle and document receipt/review of the thumb drive provided by USA Gymnastics; policy should require evidence intake logs, secure storage, and documented review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: FBI Crimes Against Children policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the FBI Crimes Against Children policy with appropriate prioritization, investigatory rigor, and coordination when allegations involve potential child sexual abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG contrasted Los Angeles’s prompt investigative steps (but failure to notify local authorities) with Indianapolis’s inaction; field offices must apply Crimes Against Children policy consistently to mitigate risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victims’ rights and victim services obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure victims’ rights are respected and that victim services are offered/available during Pre-Assessment, Assessment, and Investigative phases when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG recommended clarifying when victim services should be offered (Recommendation 1.d). FBI response indicates Victim Services Division reviewed and updated policy guidance to ensure support for trauma-informed care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reporting of child abuse to state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with federal mandatory reporting law and FBI policy requiring reporting of child abuse to state/local child protective services or law enforcement when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter on Federal Mandatory Reporting Law and FBI Policy: offices must know and follow both federal reporting obligations and FBI internal requirements to notify state/local agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid appearance of conflict of interest; seek ethics guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must avoid situations that create the appearance of a conflict of interest and must consult designated agency ethics officials before engaging with entities (or negotiating employment) that have interests in matters the employee is handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG concluded Abbott created an appearance of a conflict by discussing a U.S. Olympic Committee job with Penny while participating in conversations about the Nassar investigation; policy requires prior ethics consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on participating in matters while negotiating for employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not participate in a matter in which the employee, or an entity with which the employee is negotiating for employment, has a financial interest; follow criminal and ethics prohibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed in ethics laws section: employees must avoid participating in matters where employment negotiations or financial relationships could create conflicts or violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards on false statements and lack of candor (18 U.S.C. § 1001)
rubrics_metrics.description: False statements, lack of candor, and false or misleading statements in documents are prohibited; OIG applies preponderance of the evidence standard for misconduct determinations; criminal law (18 U.S.C. § 1001) also applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIG found Abbott and the Indianapolis SSA made materially false statements; agencies must investigate and, where appropriate, pursue administrative or criminal action. Preponderance standard cited for OIG determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisors must not approve documentation they authored
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors may not approve documentation that they themselves drafted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FBI response: new policy language will emphasize that supervisors may not approve documentation they drafted, to prevent conflicts and preserve supervisory objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve technical infrastructure for oversight of pre-investigation handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and improve technical infrastructure to enhance oversight capabilities and improve the visibility of information handling prior to the opening of an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FBI response: assess case management systems to ensure transfers, FD-71s, and pre-assessment records are discoverable and auditable.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day recurrent review period for pre-investigation information
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandate a 30-day recurrent review period for information received prior to opening an investigation to ensure timely reassessment of allegations and prompt escalation when warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FBI response: add policy to DIOG requiring periodic review of pre-investigation materials to prevent matters from languishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephonic interviews of minors only in limited exigent circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephonic interviews of minor victims should be permitted only in limited, exigent circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FBI response: DIOG update will restrict telephonic interviews of minors; OIG found telephonic interview of Gymnast 1 was poor judgment and recommended policy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory training for reporting child abuse and supervisory obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory training for all employees on obligations to report child abuse and new mandatory supervisor training for managers who oversee related investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FBI response: updated annual training now mandated for all employees; developing new mandatory supervisor training to ensure knowledge of reporting, documentation, and victim service obligations.
